summary: PARTIAL is right. Since f1be4abc7 the route bodies have been split by hand with lazyRouteComponent (60633eff3/451f35925), PreviewFileNavigationGuard is lazy, and the boot graph shrank from ~2,023 KiB raw to ~1,566 KiB raw (boot 895 KB + boot-vendor 707 KB, ~478 KiB gzip). The cost the finding describes is still there: the root beforeLoad auth (/api/auth/session plus the descriptor) starts only after the whole boot chain has downloaded and evaluated, and that chain still holds the connection runtime, wsTransport and the stores. Three of the auditor's details are wrong. (1) The BOOT_ROOT_MODULES views do not evaluate lazily: the boot chunk scope-hoists them, so they run at boot. (2) The rpc barrel in main.tsx is not a real edge to wsTransport, because client-runtime is sideEffects:false. (3) The edge cuts alone shrink nothing while BOOT_ROOT_MODULES stays, because ChatIndexRouteView imports environments/runtime directly. Since #710 the shell chunk already downloads during auth, so the remaining gain is small. Worth: low.

evidence.note: tanstackRouter() still runs with defaults (no autoCodeSplitting). vite.config.ts:220-225 passes BOOT_ROOT_MODULES as boot roots.

Bodies are lazy via lazyRouteComponent in _chat, _chat.index (:15), thread (:33), draft, projects, pull-requests, statistics, diagnostics, native.authorize and settingsRoute.ts. The route files are thin, and webBundleSplitting.test.ts:12-180 guards them. These parts of the proposal are done without autoCodeSplitting.
PreviewFileNavigationGuard is lazy. That proposal item is done.

Auth still starts here: dynamic import of the primary module, then Promise.all(ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady, resolveInitialServerAuthGateState) at :250-253. That happens only after main has evaluated, which needs boot and boot-vendor to have run. The #710 mitigations at :159-165 (shell and route chunk preload), :249 (ws-token prefetch) and :255 (early connect) overlap the work after auth, not the wait before it.
The inline module script only marks the start and imports /src/main.tsx. There is no early session or descriptor fetch.

This is the dominant chain to the runtime. utils (imported by ui/button in __root, ui/input, and RycoLetterMark/AppBootLoadingSurface) imports composerDraftStore, which leads through composerDraftPersistence, composerFileUpload, platform/attachmentUpload, environments/runtime/index, service.ts, rpc/wsRpcClient and client-runtime rpc/wsRpcClient to wsTransport. This comes from a binding-aware static walk (oxc parseSync, client-mode seams applied).
This is a second, independent path, new in 60633eff3. It goes through lib/threadDetailPrewarm.ts:3 to environments/runtime/service.

This is a third, independent path: eager pair.tsx:3-7 leads to addSavedEnvironment from environments/runtime (service plus catalog). environments/primary at :6-10 is lean now: its own closure is 16 files / 49 KB source with no wsTransport, so auth itself no longer needs the runtime.

This is not a meaningful lever. packages/client-runtime/package.json:6 sets sideEffects:false, so the export * in apps/web/src/rpc/wsConnectionState.ts:13 bundles only client-runtime rpc/wsConnectionState. Cutting main.tsx:19/38 removes about 3 files / 15 KB source. The walk results: main closure at HEAD is 281 files / 2.55 MB source. Cutting any one or two of the three paths above leaves runtime and wsTransport in. Cutting all three leaves 91 files / 0.54 MB.

BOOT_ROOT_MODULES (ChatLayoutRouteView, ChatIndexRouteView) join the boot group, because the walk queue includes the roots (:176). ChatIndexRouteView.tsx:10 imports environments/runtime directly. The main+roots closure is 342 files / 3.04 MB, and still 340 files / 3.04 MB after all three cuts. The edge cuts alone therefore change nothing in the boot chunk.

The local build is from 21:45, after HEAD at 21:40. The roots evaluate at boot, not on first use: `var KCe=e({ChatLayoutRoute:()=>XCe})` is hoisted to the top level, and the route component is `Promise.resolve().then(()=>KCe)`. rolldown-runtime exports only __commonJS/__export/__toESM, and no lazy ESM init exists. Sizes: boot 894,988 B (261 KB gz), boot-vendor 707,326 B (229 KB gz), main 922 B. RootAppShell is 341,660 B and is fetched after boot.

This comment and standardBootGraph.test.ts:170-172 claim the roots 'evaluate on first use', which is wrong given the dist. codeSplitting.ts:147 refers to a non-existent HOSTED_BOOT_ROOT_MODULES. The auditor repeated the 'evaluate lazily' claim.

The code records that preloading later phases at document start delayed the root beforeLoad through contention, and codeSplitting.ts:273-275 records a +0.35 s hosted cost for a separate chunk. Measured evidence exists against both obvious ways of moving the shell closure out of boot.

No rule forbids environments/runtime, wsTransport or composerDraftStore in main.tsx's graph. The walker is not barrel- or binding-aware, so a wsTransport rule would false-positive through main.tsx:19. The scripts/perf/model.ts:260-275 boot budget (520 KiB gzip) has no forbidden rule for these modules either.

remaining: The root beforeLoad auth (apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:239-253) still waits for the full boot chain (~1.57 MiB raw / ~478 KiB gzip) to download and evaluate, and that chain contains the connection runtime, wsTransport, contracts and stores. Three independent static paths put them in main's closure: lib/utils.ts:4 -> composerDraftStore -> ... -> environments/runtime -> wsTransport; routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:5-8 -> lib/threadDetailPrewarm.ts:3 -> environments/runtime/service; and routes/pair.tsx:3-7 -> components/auth/PairingRouteSurface.tsx:5 -> environments/runtime. All three must be cut to remove them. Even then the boot chunk does not change, because BOOT_ROOT_MODULES (viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:277-280) pulls the same closure back into boot through ChatIndexRouteView.tsx:10, and those modules evaluate at boot. index.html:128-131 has no early session fetch. The seed call at main.tsx:19/38 is not a real cost. Since #710 the shell chunk downloads during auth, so the user-visible gain left is about min(auth RTT, boot download+eval). That is a few ms on loopback, up to one RTT on a remote standard node with warm caches.
fixDefects: No functional defect in the route splitting. Three doc/guard defects: (1) codeSplitting.ts:271-272 and standardBootGraph.test.ts:170-172 say BOOT_ROOT_MODULES 'evaluate on first use/when the router first renders them', but the build scope-hoists them into boot and evaluates them before auth. The measured trade-off comment therefore misdescribes its own cost, and codeSplitting.ts:147 cites a non-existent HOSTED_BOOT_ROOT_MODULES. (2) The new eager threadDetailPrewarm import (thread route :5-8) adds a third independent path to environments/runtime/service, and no boot-graph rule catches it. (3) The await import() calls at __root.tsx:203, :215, :244, :276, :316 and :343 target modules that sit inside the boot chunk, so they split nothing. This is cosmetic, but it only becomes a real split once the paths are cut.
implementationSketch:
Option A, cheapest. Standard builds only; never hosted (AGENTS.md hosted lifecycle owner), never Electron, never with VITE_HTTP_URL set.
- apps/web/index.html:95-132: in the inline module script, when VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE !== 'hosted-hub', the page is same-origin http(s) and not desktop, and the pathname is not /pair and does not start with /native/authorize/, start fetch('/api/auth/session', {credentials:'same-origin'}) and the primary descriptor request that ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady makes. Catch errors to null and stash {requestedAt, session, descriptor} on one global.
- packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts: add an optional deps.takeBootSessionPrefetch(). The first fetchSessionState inside bootstrapServerAuth (:239-255) adopts it exactly once, mirroring prefetchPrimaryWebSocketToken/discard at :303-312. Accept only ok and fresh responses; fall back to the normal retrying fetch on null, non-ok or stale. Do the same in the descriptor bootstrap.
- The web platform adapter provides the take function; the hosted adapter does not.
- Tests: unit tests for primaryAuth adoption (adopted once, 401/500/network fallback, reset clears it); a build test that the hosted index.html contains no prefetch; a browser test that a standard boot issues exactly one /api/auth/session.

Option B, structural. Needs fresh measurements on both the hosted 150 ms/1.6 Mbps profile and standard loopback.
- Move the DraftId schema out of composerDraftStore into a dependency-free module and fix lib/utils.ts:4.
- In the thread route loader, reach retainThreadDetailSubscription through a tiny registry module that dynamically imports environments/runtime/service. Keep releaseThreadDetailPrewarmsExcept synchronous.
- In PairingRouteSurface, load addSavedEnvironment with await import('../../environments/runtime') inside the submit handler. Keep environments/primary static, since it is lean.
- Then stop grouping BOOT_ROOT_MODULES into boot, or make them a separate chunk preloaded with low priority. Without the cuts and this change, the cuts gain nothing.
- Guard it in standardBootGraph.test.ts with forbiddenChains('main.tsx', [environments/runtime/(service|connection).ts, composerDraftStore.ts, client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts]). First make the walker skip pure re-export barrels of sideEffects:false packages (as createBootGraphMatcher already does), or have main.tsx import seedWsConnectionOnlineStatus from a narrow module.
- Add the same patterns to the boot forbiddenSources in scripts/perf/model.ts.

In either case, fix the comments at codeSplitting.ts:147 and :271-272 and standardBootGraph.test.ts:170-172 so they say the roots evaluate at boot.
decisionReason: A real gain needs one of two things. One is reversing the measured BOOT_ROOT_MODULES trade-off (+0.35 s hosted sign-in, ~30 ms standard paint), against document-start preload contention that is also measured. The other is issuing the auth session/descriptor request from index.html, outside the client-runtime auth owner, which must stay standard-only under the hosted lifecycle rules. Since #710 the remaining benefit is a few ms locally and at most one RTT on remote warm-cache boots, so the owner should decide whether it is worth doing at all.
correction: The auditor was wrong on several points. (1) 'They evaluate lazily but are downloaded at boot' is wrong: the dist shows the ChatLayout/ChatIndex closures scope-hoisted into boot with no lazy init, so they evaluate before auth, and the source comments that say otherwise are wrong too. (2) The claim that main.tsx:19/38's rpc barrel pulls in wsTransport is wrong for the bundle: client-runtime is sideEffects:false and only wsConnectionState is bundled, so moving the seed call saves about 15 KB source and is not a lever. (3) Their cheapest-first order is misleading. Cutting the edges in step 2 gives zero boot-chunk change while BOOT_ROOT_MODULES remains, because ChatIndexRouteView.tsx:10 imports environments/runtime directly (342 vs 340 files). Step 4 is therefore required for any gain from step 2, not optional. (4) They described the utils.ts:4 edge only as 'composer draft store in boot', but it is the shortest and dominant chain to environments/runtime and wsTransport (via composerDraftPersistence -> composerFileUpload -> platform/attachmentUpload). All three edges must be cut together; any single cut changes almost nothing. (5) environments/primary is now lean (16 files / 49 KB, no wsTransport), unlike the original verifier's 519 KiB primary closure. (6) BOOT_ROOT_MODULES is at codeSplitting.ts:277, not :254.
